# Business Suite — multi-app business platform

A Persian-first (RTL, Jalali calendar, business-selected money display) multi-industry platform with **four standalone apps**: Accounting, Growth & Marketing, CRM, and Website Management. Accounting includes sales/POS, operations, inventory and reporting. Website Management contains two separate SaaS managers, Eshobe CMS and WordPress/WooCommerce. AI, settings and connections are shared platform services. The industry profile adapts the work areas for hospitality, retail, jewelry, cosmetics, wholesale and other supported businesses. See [the app boundaries](docs/app-boundaries.md).

Development history and shipped capability are documented in [docs/phases/README.md](docs/phases/README.md). Early phases began with café/restaurant POS workflows; later phases evolved that foundation into the current multi-industry, multi-app business platform. Phase documents are historical implementation records, not the current product definition.

## Stack

- **Next.js 15** (App Router, TypeScript) — single app, role-based routes
- **PostgreSQL 16** — full schema for all phases migrated up front
- **Tailwind CSS 4** — logical properties for RTL-safe layout
- **Vazirmatn** variable font (bundled locally, works offline)
- Auth: **JWT session cookie** (Owner/Manager email+password) + **4–12-digit PIN quick-login** (Cashier/Waiter/Kitchen)

## Getting started

```bash
# 1. Start Postgres (Docker)
docker compose up -d

# 2. Configure environment
cp .env.example .env    # defaults match docker-compose

# 3. Install, migrate
npm install
npm run db:migrate

# 4. Run
npm run dev             # http://localhost:3000
```

### First run — the Setup Wizard (Phase 1)

On a **completely empty database**, opening the app sends you to `/welcome`, which
creates the business + first Owner account, then walks you through the guided
wizard (`/setup/*`) — no manual DB edits needed. The step sequence is
industry-shaped (`src/lib/wizard-steps.ts` is the one place that decides it):

- **Food service (کافه و رستوران)** — the full path:

  1. **Business info** — name, location, currency/language defaults
  2. **Chart of accounts** — editable pre-built F&B template
  3. **Inventory costing** — FIFO/LIFO/Weighted Average, perpetual vs periodic (locked after the first inventory transaction)
  4. **Tax** — default VAT rate + per-category rates
  5. **Roles & users** — Manager (email/password) and Cashier/Waiter/Kitchen (4–12-digit PIN) *(optional)*
  6. **Menu** — manual entry or CSV/Excel import (downloadable template). The step is only ready once at least one active item exists.
  7. **Hardware** — printer pairing + test print, the *same* panel as Settings → Printers. On the desktop app printing goes straight through Electron; in a browser/cloud till the panel installs the one-click Windows print connector. *(optional)*
  8. **Backup destination** — local-only installs, with a real OS folder dialog *(optional)*
  9. **Opening balances** — opening inventory count + balanced opening journal entry *(optional)*

- **Trade-goods retail (طلا و جواهر، ساعت، بدلیجات، آرایشی، عمده‌فروشی، ابزار، خرازی)** —
  the same path without costing and menu: the catalogue is managed in the products
  workspace (`/accounting/products`, or the trade's own items page), and the wizard's
  finish page points at it.
- **Services / SaaS** — business info, chart of accounts, tax, then the optional
  users/hardware/backup/opening steps.

A standalone desktop install also has `/welcome` ask whether to set up locally or pair
with an existing online business
([docs/standalone-desktop-app.md](docs/standalone-desktop-app.md#first-run--local-setup-or-pairing));
pairing imports an already-configured business and marks setup complete outright.

Until `POST /api/setup/complete` stamps the completion marker (the Finish step), Owner/
Manager logins are routed into the wizard; the dashboard shows a "resume setup" banner.
Reaching a required step does *not* end the wizard on its own — Hardware, Backup,
Opening and Finish stay reachable for every industry. Businesses created ready-to-use by
the platform console (and the demo seed) are stamped complete up front, so they never
enter onboarding.

### Optional: seed a demo business instead

To skip the wizard and get a ready-to-log-in demo:

```bash
npm run db:seed         # creates owner@example.com / owner1234 and a cashier with PIN 1234
```

Log in (the two doors are separate pages):

- **Owner/Manager:** `/admin` — `owner@example.com` / `owner1234` (override via `SEED_OWNER_*` env vars before seeding)
- **Staff quick login:** `/login` — PIN `1234` (sample cashier)

The seed also creates 3 sample dining tables and a small demo menu (2 categories, 3 items,
1 modifier group) so the cashier POS screen has something to sell right away.

### Menu management & the cashier POS (Phase 2)

- **`/accounting/menu`** (Owner/Manager) — CRUD for categories, items, modifier groups and
  modifiers, plus attaching modifier groups to items with per-item min/max overrides and
  item-specific ordering. Independent of the wizard's initial import — ongoing management.
  The retired `/dashboard/menu` and `/settings/menu` addresses are permanent redirects here.
- **`/accounting/pos`** (Owner/Manager/Cashier) — the cashier screen: category tabs → item
  grid → cart with per-item modifiers, quantity, and an order-level discount (percent or
  fixed amount). Choose dine-in (pick a table from the stub list) or takeaway (gets a
  queue number, e.g. `T-42`), then submit.
- **`/dashboard/orders`** — open orders list and detail view; while an order is `open` you
  can add items, change quantity, void an item, edit the discount, or void the whole order.

### Waiter app & Kitchen Display (Phase 4)

Orders sync live over a WebSocket (`/ws`, see `server.ts` + `src/lib/realtime.ts`) — no
polling. Submitting an order (from the cashier POS or the waiter app) *is* "send to
kitchen": its items land on the KDS as `sent` immediately.

- **`/dashboard/waiter`** (Waiter, + Owner/Manager "all tables" overview) — only the
  sections assigned to the logged-in waiter (`floor_sections.assigned_waiter_id`, set on
  the floor plan). Tap a seated table to add items to its open order/round, see each
  item's live kitchen status, and mark a `ready` item `served` once it's delivered.
- **`/accounting/kitchen`** (Kitchen, + Owner/Manager) — the KDS: one ticket per table
  (grouping every round on that table's open session) or per takeaway order. Its deterministic
  next-ticket queue places overdue tickets first, then `sent`, `preparing`, and `ready`, with
  oldest-first ties—no AI call or credit charge. Tickets outstanding ≥ 10 minutes
  (`DEFAULT_TICKET_AGING_MINUTES`, `src/lib/order-item-status.ts`) flag red. "Bump" moves an
  item `sent → preparing → ready`.
- Every open dashboard screen (cashier orders list, floor plan, waiter board, KDS)
  refetches on the relevant WebSocket event, so no two screens ever show conflicting
  order/table state.

394	## Overview
395	
396	Vercel is a developer-platform brand — the page is a deployment dashboard's marketing surface, written for engineers who already know the syntax. It earns that posture with one of the cleanest stark systems on the web: near-white `{colors.canvas-soft}` body background, ink-near-black `{colors.ink}` text, a 200-step gray scale that gives every divider, border, and disabled state its own deliberate step. The only place the brand introduces colour at marketing scale is the multi-stop mesh gradient (`{colors.gradient-develop-start}` → `{colors.gradient-preview-end}` → `{colors.gradient-ship-start}` → cyan / magenta / amber) that floats in atmospheric backdrops, never miniaturised to a swatch. That gradient is the entire decoration system.
397	
398	Type is the second decisive voice. The brand's own custom geometric sans (Geist) carries display, body, button — everything narrative — at weight 600 for display, 500 for buttons, 400 for body. A matching monospaced face (Geist Mono) carries technical labels: terminal mockups, code blocks, sometimes filename captions. Headlines are sentence-case with aggressive negative letter-spacing (`-2.4px` at 48 px hero) — the brand never letter-spaces positively, never goes uppercase outside of mono labels.
399	
400	Surfaces use a four-step ladder: `{colors.canvas}` (pure white for cards), `{colors.canvas-soft}` 98% (the page body), `{colors.canvas-soft-2}` 95% (occasional inset region), `{colors.primary}` (the deep ink-near-black used as the polarity-flipped band when a section needs the dark mode treatment). Shadows are exceptionally subtle — every elevated card carries a stacked shadow built from `0px 1px 1px #00000005` + `0px 2px 2px #0000000a` + an inset border. Cards never float on heavy drop-shadow; they sit on the page held by hairline + soft glow.
401	
402	**Key Characteristics:**
403	- A single black-ink primary CTA `{colors.primary}` carries every conversion target, paired with white-on-white `button-secondary` for the secondary action. The brand uses 100 px pill shape for marketing CTAs and a tight 6 px square shape for in-app nav buttons.
404	- A multi-stop mesh gradient (cyan-blue-magenta-amber) is the only decorative chrome — used at hero scale and inside feature-band atmospheric backdrops. It is the brand.
405	- Every section eyebrow and small label uses the monospace face `{typography.caption-mono}` or `{typography.code}`; everything else is in the geometric sans.
406	- Subtle stacked-shadow elevation — three offsets layered with 4-12 % black opacity — never a single heavy drop-shadow.
407	- A complete 100–1000 gray + blue + red + amber + green + teal + purple + pink colour scale exists as a system token set, but the marketing surface uses only the `100`, `1000`, and `700`-level tones; the rest stay in the design-system tokens for in-product surfaces.
408	- An "Active CPU" pricing rhythm: `pricing-card` lays out 3-up on the pricing page with `pricing-card-featured` (Pro tier) polarity-flipped to `{colors.primary}` against white-card siblings.
409	
410	## Colors
411	
412	### Brand & Accent
413	- **Ink** (`{colors.primary}` — `#171717`): The single primary CTA color. Black-near-pure ink that carries every Sign Up pill, every footer CTA, the dark-band polarity-flip. Used as text color throughout the page on light surfaces. (Resolved from `--ds-gray-1000`.)
414	- **Cyan** (`{colors.cyan}` — `#50e3c2`): A signature mint-cyan used in the brand gradient and inside Geist-system spotlight tokens. Visible inside the hero gradient stops.
415	- **Highlight Pink** (`{colors.highlight-pink}` — `#ff0080`): The brand's highlight magenta, used as the high-saturation stop in the preview-gradient pair.
416	- **Violet** (`{colors.violet}` — `#7928ca`): The deep purple used as the start of the preview-gradient and inside developer-console highlights.
417	- **Link Blue** (`{colors.link}` — `#0070f3`): The brand's primary link color and the legacy `--geist-success` semantic.
418	
419	### Surface
420	- **Canvas** (`{colors.canvas}` — `#ffffff`): The pure-white card / dialog / modal surface.
421	- **Canvas Soft** (`{colors.canvas-soft}` — `#fafafa`): The default page background — 98 % white. Almost every section sits on this tone.
422	- **Canvas Soft 2** (`{colors.canvas-soft-2}` — `#f5f5f5`): A slightly deeper inset surface for "code editor inner background", template-card hover states, and dropdown menus.
423	- **Hairline** (`{colors.hairline}` — `#ebebeb`): 1 px dividers — table rows, card borders, input borders.
424	- **Hairline Strong** (`{colors.hairline-strong}` — `#a1a1a1`): The 500-level gray, used as the slightly-stronger divider on light bands and as the deemphasised text color.
425	
426	### Text
427	- **Ink** (`{colors.ink}` — `#171717`): Every heading and body paragraph on light surfaces.
428	- **Body** (`{colors.body}` — `#4d4d4d`): Secondary text — sub-headings, body captions, nav-link inactive text, footer column body.
429	- **Mute** (`{colors.mute}` — `#888888`): Lowest-priority text — placeholder text, fine print, low-key labels.
430	- **On Primary** (`{colors.on-primary}` — `#ffffff`): All text on `{colors.primary}` surfaces.
431	
432	### Semantic
433	- **Success / Link** (`{colors.success}` — `#0070f3`): The brand's legacy success indicator doubles as the primary link color. Visible underline-on-hover for inline body links.
434	- **Link Deep** (`{colors.link-deep}` — `#0761d1`): The pressed / visited tone for inline links.
435	- **Link Bg Soft** (`{colors.link-bg-soft}` — `#d3e5ff`): Soft pastel blue fill for "what's new" pill banners and informational badges.
436	- **Error** (`{colors.error}` — `#ee0000`): Validation red for destructive actions and form errors.
437	- **Error Soft** (`{colors.error-soft}` — `#f7d4d6`): Soft pastel red for destructive-state backgrounds.
438	- **Error Deep** (`{colors.error-deep}` — `#c50000`): Pressed / deep destructive state.
439	- **Warning** (`{colors.warning}` — `#f5a623`): Caution / pending status indicator.
440	- **Warning Soft** (`{colors.warning-soft}` — `#ffefcf`) / **Warning Deep** (`{colors.warning-deep}` — `#ab570a`): Background + pressed variants.
441	
442	### Brand Gradient
443	The brand's signature decoration is a three-pair gradient stack:
444	- **Develop** (`{colors.gradient-develop-start}` `#007cf0` → `{colors.gradient-develop-end}` `#00dfd8`) — the blue-to-teal pair used to mark the "deploy" / "develop" rhythm.
445	- **Preview** (`{colors.gradient-preview-start}` `#7928ca` → `{colors.gradient-preview-end}` `#ff0080`) — the violet-to-pink pair used for "preview" surfaces.
446	- **Ship** (`{colors.gradient-ship-start}` `#ff4d4d` → `{colors.gradient-ship-end}` `#f9cb28`) — the coral-to-amber pair used for "ship" surfaces.
447	
448	The three pairs collapse into a single multi-color mesh gradient when used as the hero atmospheric backdrop. Treat the gradient as one unified object — do not crop down to a single colour, do not reorder the stops, and do not miniaturise. Used at hero scale only.
449	
450	## Typography
451	
452	### Font Family
453	Two custom faces carry the entire system:
454	
455	1. **A custom geometric sans** (extracted as `Geist`) for every display, body, button, link, and label. Weights 400 / 500 / 600 are the working set; the face never appears in 700 or heavier. Display sizes are tracked aggressively negative (`-2.4 px` at 48 px hero, `-1.28 px` at 32 px section); body stays at neutral or slightly-negative tracking.
456	2. **A custom monospaced face** (extracted as `Geist Mono`) for terminal mockups, code blocks, and small mono-caption labels — anything that wants to signal "technical." Weight 400 only at 12 – 13 px. Tracking neutral.
457	
458	A condensed display sans (`Space Grotesk`) is loaded as a third face for occasional editorial moments but does not render as the primary face anywhere in the captured surfaces.
459	
460	### Hierarchy
461	
462	| Token | Size | Weight | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Use |
463	|---|---|---|---|---|---|
464	| `{typography.display-xl}` | 48px | 600 | 48px | -2.4px | Hero headline ("Build and deploy on the AI Cloud."). |
465	| `{typography.display-lg}` | 32px | 600 | 40px | -1.28px | Section headlines ("Your frontend, delivered.", "A compute model for all workloads."). |
466	| `{typography.display-md}` | 24px | 600 | 32px | -0.96px | Card-cluster headlines, pricing-tier names. |
467	| `{typography.display-sm}` | 20px | 600 | 28px | -0.6px | Inline display micro-headings. |
468	| `{typography.body-lg}` | 18px | 400 | 28px | 0 | Lead paragraphs under section headlines. |
469	| `{typography.body-md}` | 16px | 400 | 24px | 0 | Default body paragraph. |
470	| `{typography.body-md-strong}` | 16px | 500 | 24px | 0 | Bolded inline body. |
471	| `{typography.body-sm}` | 14px | 400 | 20px | -0.28px | Secondary body, nav-link text, button-md labels. |
472	| `{typography.body-sm-strong}` | 14px | 500 | 20px | -0.28px | Nav CTA labels, table-row emphasis. |
473	| `{typography.caption}` | 12px | 400 | 16px | 0 | Footer secondary lines, badge labels. |
474	| `{typography.caption-mono}` | 12px | 400 | 16px | 0 | Section eyebrows and label captions that want a technical voice. |
475	| `{typography.code}` | 13px | 400 | 20px | 0 | Inline code, terminal mockups, command snippets. |
476	| `{typography.button-md}` | 14px | 500 | 20px | 0 | Small / nav-scale button labels. |
477	| `{typography.button-lg}` | 16px | 500 | 24px | 0 | Marketing-scale pill button labels. |
478	
479	### Principles
480	- **Negative tracking is part of the voice.** Display sizes use aggressive `-2.4` to `-0.6` px tracking. Reverting to default tracking breaks the brand.
481	- **Sentence-case headlines, period-terminated.** Headlines like "Build and deploy on the AI Cloud." end with a deliberate period — that punctuation is part of the brand's voice.
482	- **Mono for the technical layer only.** Section eyebrows, code blocks, terminal mockups. Body paragraphs never set in mono.
483	- **Weight 600 is the display ceiling.** The geometric sans never appears at 700 / 800. The brand reads as a calmer system because of this.
484	
485	### Note on Font Substitutes
486	The two primary faces are proprietary (custom-cut for the brand). Open-source substitutes:
487	- **Geometric sans** — *Inter* (400 / 500 / 600) is the closest stylistic match; `font-feature-settings: "ss01", "ss02"` enables the geometric alternates. *Satoshi* is a passable second choice.
488	- **Monospace** — *JetBrains Mono* (400) at 12 – 13 px matches the technical voice. *IBM Plex Mono* is the second-best option.
489	
490	## Layout
491	
492	### Spacing System
493	- **Base unit**: 4 px. The brand's `--geist-space` token is exactly 4 px and every captured value is a multiple of 4.
494	- **Tokens**: `{spacing.xxs}` 4 px · `{spacing.xs}` 8 px · `{spacing.sm}` 12 px · `{spacing.md}` 16 px · `{spacing.lg}` 24 px · `{spacing.xl}` 32 px · `{spacing.2xl}` 40 px · `{spacing.3xl}` 48 px · `{spacing.4xl}` 64 px · `{spacing.5xl}` 96 px · `{spacing.6xl}` 128 px · `{spacing.section}` 192 px.
495	- **Section padding**: marketing bands use `{spacing.4xl}` to `{spacing.5xl}` top/bottom. Hero bands stretch to `{spacing.section}` to give the mesh gradient room to breathe.
496	- **Card interior padding**: marketing cards sit at `{spacing.lg}` to `{spacing.xl}`; template-grid cards stay tighter at `{spacing.md}` because they sit in a denser grid.
497	- **Inline gap**: button rows, nav rows, and chip rows use `{spacing.sm}` to `{spacing.md}` between siblings. The brand's `--geist-gap` is exactly 24 px.
498	
499	### Grid & Container
500	- **Max width**: ~1400 px (`--ds-page-width`); the legacy `--geist-page-width` is 1200 px and still appears on some marketing surfaces. Content centres with horizontal gutters of `{spacing.lg}` 24 px on desktop, `{spacing.md}` 16 px on mobile.
501	- **Column patterns**:
502	  - Three-feature row: 3-up at desktop, 1-up at mobile (rows like "Web Apps / Composable Commerce / Multi-tenant Platforms").
503	  - Tab pill row: 5-up centred row of `tab-ghost` pills.
504	  - Template-grid cluster: 5-up at desktop, scaling to 1-up at mobile.
505	  - Pricing tier grid: 3-up at desktop with the middle tier polarity-flipped.
506	  - Logo strip: ~5 logos wide, single row.
507	
508	### Whitespace Philosophy
509	The mesh gradient does most of the heavy decorative lifting; whitespace separates the bands. Section spacing is generous — `{spacing.4xl}` to `{spacing.5xl}` between bands lets the gradient breathe. Inside a card, the headline/paragraph stack is tight (`{spacing.xs}` 8 px gap), then a wider gap before the CTA cluster. The page reads as engineered — large gaps + tight interior, never the other way around.
510	
511	### Responsive Strategy
512	
513	#### Breakpoints
514	
515	| Name | Width | Key Changes |
516	|---|---|---|
517	| Mobile | < 600px | Hero stacks; nav collapses to hamburger; 3-up feature grids drop to 1-up; tab pill row enables horizontal scroll. |
518	| Tablet | 600–959px | 3-up grids drop to 2-up; nav still horizontal. |
519	| Desktop | 960–1199px | Full 3-up grids; pricing 3-up. |
520	| Wide | 1200–1399px | Container caps at 1400 px content width. |
521	| Ultra-wide | ≥ 1400px | Content stays centred at 1400 px; bands stretch edge-to-edge in colour but content holds the max-width. |
522	
523	#### Touch Targets
524	The `button-primary` pill renders at ~32 px tall in nav and ~48 px tall in marketing contexts. Marketing CTAs comfortably meet WCAG AAA at all breakpoints; nav buttons inflate touch area through `{spacing.xs}` padding on mobile to meet the 44 × 44 px floor.
525	
526	#### Collapsing Strategy
527	- **Nav**: full link row + Ask AI / Log In / Sign Up pills at desktop. Collapses to logo + hamburger at mobile with the menu opening as a full-overlay.
528	- **Hero**: mesh gradient stays centred; headline + body stack vertically at all breakpoints (the brand doesn't use a split-hero pattern).
529	- **Three-feature row**: 3-up → 2-up → 1-up at the breakpoints above; cards keep their `{rounded.md}` 8 px shape across all viewports.
530	- **Pricing card grid**: 3-up at desktop, vertical stack at mobile with `pricing-card-featured` always sitting in the middle.
531	- **Template grid**: 5-up → 3-up → 2-up → 1-up. Each `template-card` keeps its 16:9 aspect on the image.
532	
533	#### Image Behavior
534	- **Mesh gradient**: rendered as inline SVG or canvas-painted gradient; scales fluidly with the hero container; never crops, never tiles.
535	- **Customer logos**: rendered as monochrome SVGs in the logo strip; consistent 24 px height.
536	- **Code editor mockup**: dark `{colors.primary}` rectangle with mono text rendered inside; treated as an image at the layout level.
537	- **Template thumbnails**: 16:9 landscape inside `{rounded.md}` card chrome; lazy-loaded; consistent grayscale palette in the placeholder state.
538	
539	## Elevation & Depth
540	
541	| Level | Treatment | Use |
542	|---|---|---|
543	| Level 0 — Flat | No shadow, no border. | Full-bleed hero bands and the polarity-flipped dark sections. |
544	| Level 1 — Inset Hairline | `0 0 0 1px #00000014` inset 1 px border. | Default card chrome — the brand's universal "you can see this card" cue. |
545	| Level 2 — Subtle Drop | `0px 1px 1px #00000005, 0px 2px 2px #0000000a` plus inset hairline. | Slightly elevated cards (template-grid, marketing-card). |
546	| Level 3 — Soft Stack | `0px 2px 2px #0000000a, 0px 8px 8px -8px #0000000a` plus inset hairline. | The "medium" elevation — feature-grid cards. |
547	| Level 4 — Float Stack | `0px 2px 2px #0000000a, 0px 8px 16px -4px #0000000a` plus inset hairline. | "Large" elevation — pricing cards, callout panels. |
548	| Level 5 — Modal | `0px 1px 1px #00000005, 0px 8px 16px -4px #0000000a, 0px 24px 32px -8px #0000000f` plus inset hairline. | Modal / dialog surfaces and dropdown menus. |
549	
550	The brand uses STACKED shadows — multiple small offsets layered to fake natural light — never a single 8-px-blur generic drop. Inset hairline rings are always added so the card edge stays crisp.
551	
552	### Decorative Depth
553	- **Mesh gradient as atmospheric depth**: the hero's multi-stop gradient is the brand's only "atmospheric" effect — applied as a flat 2-D backdrop rather than a 3-D illustration.
554	- **Polarity-flipped dark band as section-depth**: switching the surface from `{colors.canvas-soft}` to `{colors.primary}` (the deep ink) is the brand's chief depth cue between bands.
555	- **Inset-shadow + drop-shadow combo**: the cards' combination of an inset 1 px ring and a multi-stop drop produces a "card sits on the page" effect without ever feeling material-heavy.
556	
557	## Shapes
558	
559	### Border Radius Scale
560	
561	| Token | Value | Use |
562	|---|---|---|
563	| `{rounded.none}` | 0px | Full-bleed hero / footer bands. |
564	| `{rounded.xs}` | 4px | Tightest inline pill — the `nav-cta-signup` 6-px-radius button (mapped to `xs/sm`). |
565	| `{rounded.sm}` | 6px | The brand's `--geist-radius` token — base UI radius for in-app buttons, form inputs, dropdown menus. |
566	| `{rounded.md}` | 8px | The brand's `--geist-marketing-radius` token — feature cards, template cards. |
567	| `{rounded.lg}` | 12px | Slightly larger card chrome (pricing-card variants). |
568	| `{rounded.xl}` | 16px | Largest card chrome — when a card hosts a hero image cap. |
569	| `{rounded.pill-sm}` | 64px | Tab-ghost pills inside the "AI Apps / Web Apps / Ecommerce / Marketing / Platforms" row. |
570	| `{rounded.pill}` | 100px | The marketing CTA pill — `button-primary`, `button-secondary`, "Start Deploying" pill. |
571	| `{rounded.full}` | 9999px | Icon-button circular containers, nav-link ghost pills. |
572	
573	### Photography Geometry
574	- **Mesh gradient**: full-bleed 2-D atmospheric backdrop, never cropped to a frame; treated as the page's wallpaper.
575	- **Customer logos**: monochrome SVG, consistent 24 px height in a flex row.
576	- **Code editor mockup**: 16:10 dark rectangle, `{rounded.md}` corners.
577	- **Template thumbnails**: 16:9 landscape inside `{rounded.md}` chrome.
578	- **Showcase imagery**: 2:1 or 16:9 inside `{rounded.lg}` to `{rounded.xl}` chrome with a stacked shadow.

707	- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`
708	
709	**`ex-modal-card`** — Modal dialog surface — same chrome as feature-card with elevated shadow.
710	- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`
711	
712	**`ex-empty-state-card`** — Empty-state illustration frame.
713	- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `captionTypography`
714	
715	**`ex-toast`** — Toast notification surface — feature-card shape + medium shadow.
716	- Properties: `backgroundColor`, `rounded`, `padding`, `typography`
717	
718	
719	## Do's and Don'ts
720	
721	### Do
722	- Reserve `{colors.primary}` (`#171717`) for primary CTAs across the page. Black ink IS the conversion target.
723	- Use `{rounded.pill}` 100 px for every marketing-scale CTA and `{rounded.sm}` 6 px for nav-scale buttons. The two pill scales coexist deliberately.
724	- Set every headline in `{typography.display-*}` weight 600, sentence-case, often period-terminated. Aggressive negative tracking is part of the voice.
725	- Use the brand mesh gradient as atmospheric decoration at hero scale only — never miniaturise it to an icon, never reduce to a single colour.
726	- Layer stacked shadows (multiple small offsets with inset hairline) rather than single heavy drops. The brand's elevation is calmer than Material.
727	- Cycle page surfaces in `{colors.canvas-soft}` → `{colors.canvas}` → `{colors.primary}` polarity-flipped bands; the dark band IS the depth cue.
728	- Set every code block and technical eyebrow in `{typography.code}` / `{typography.caption-mono}`. Mono is the voice of the platform.
729	
730	### Don't
731	- Don't introduce a sixth accent colour. The brand operates with ink + gray + the four-pair gradient palette; new accents flatten the voice.
732	- Don't render headlines in all-caps. Sentence-case + negative tracking is non-negotiable.
733	- Don't drop a single heavy drop-shadow on cards. The brand's elevation is built from stacked small offsets + inset hairline rings.
734	- Don't render the brand gradient at icon scale or in a single-colour reduced form. The gradient lives at hero scale only.
735	- Don't promote the geometric sans to weight 700. The brand's display ceiling is 600.
736	- Don't pair the marketing 100-px pill CTA shape with the 6-px nav radius on the same screen — pick a scale and stay there.
737	- Don't set body paragraphs in the mono face. The mono is for code + technical labels only.
738	
739	</design-context>
740	
741	Use the design system above for all UI you generate.
742	
743	---
744	
745	<skill-context>
746	---
747	name: design-taste-frontend
748	description: Anti-slop frontend skill for landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. The agent reads the brief, infers the right design direction, and ships interfaces that do not look templated. Real design systems when applicable, audit-first on redesigns, strict pre-flight check.
749	---
750	
751	# tasteskill: Anti-Slop Frontend Skill
752	
753	> Landing pages, portfolios, and redesigns. Not dashboards, not data tables, not multi-step product UI.
754	> Every rule below is **contextual**. None of it fires automatically. First read the brief, then pull only what fits.
755	
756	---
757	
758	## 0. BRIEF INFERENCE (Read the Room Before Anything Else)
759	
760	Before touching code or tweaking dials, **infer what the user actually wants**. Most LLM design output is bad because the model jumps to a default aesthetic instead of reading the room.
761	
762	### 0.A Read these signals first
763	1. **Page kind** - landing (SaaS / consumer / agency / event), portfolio (dev / designer / creative studio), redesign (preserve vs overhaul), editorial / blog.
764	2. **Vibe words** the user used - "minimalist", "calm", "Linear-style", "Awwwards", "brutalist", "premium consumer", "Apple-y", "playful", "serious B2B", "editorial", "agency-y", "glassy", "dark tech".
765	3. **Reference signals** - URLs they linked, screenshots they pasted, products they named, brands they're competing with.
766	4. **Audience** - B2B procurement panel vs. design-conscious consumer vs. recruiter scanning a portfolio. The audience picks the aesthetic, not your taste.
767	5. **Brand assets that already exist** - logo, color, type, photography. For redesigns, these are starting material, not optional input (see Section 11).
768	6. **Quiet constraints** - accessibility-first audiences, public-sector, regulated industries, trust-first commerce, kids' products. These constraints OVERRIDE aesthetic preference.
769	
770	### 0.B Output a one-line "Design Read" before generating
771	Before any code, state in one line: **"Reading this as: \<page kind> for \<audience>, with a \<vibe> language, leaning toward \<design system or aesthetic family>."**
772	
773	Example reads:
774	- *"Reading this as: B2B SaaS landing for technical buyers, with a Linear-style minimalist language, leaning toward Tailwind utilities + Geist + restrained motion."*
775	- *"Reading this as: solo designer portfolio for hiring managers, with an editorial / kinetic-type language, leaning toward native CSS + scroll-driven animation + custom typography."*
776	- *"Reading this as: redesign of a public-sector service site, with a trust-first language, leaning toward GOV.UK Frontend or USWDS."*
777	
778	### 0.C If the brief is ambiguous, ask one question, do not guess
779	Ask exactly **one** clarifying question - never a multi-question dump - and only when the design read genuinely diverges. Example: *"Should this feel closer to Linear-clean or Awwwards-experimental?"*
780	
781	If you can confidently infer from context, **do not ask**. Just declare the design read and proceed.
782	
783	### 0.D Anti-Default Discipline
784	Do not default to: AI-purple gradients, centered hero over dark mesh, three equal feature cards, generic glassmorphism on everything, infinite-loop micro-animations everywhere, Inter + slate-900. These are the LLM defaults. Reach past them deliberately based on the design read.
785

2	
3	**For AI agents and human developers building headless themes (including ecommerce).**
4	
5	*Version: `contractVersion = 1` — `GET /api/site` returns this number. Bump = breaking change.*

35	
36	## 1. Theme Repository Quick Start for an AI Agent
37	
38	Build a compatible theme repository in this order. Eshobe does **not** require a
39	specific frontend framework; these steps work for Next, Remix, SvelteKit, Astro, a
40	plain Node server, or any app that can answer HTTP.
41	
42	1. Create an application that can render HTML for a site.
43	2. Install the runtime helpers: `pnpm add @eshobe/site-runtime`.
44	3. Add `eshobe.theme.json` at the repository root (full spec in §17b).
45	4. Implement a CMS client that uses either same-origin `/api/*`, or `ESHOBE_CMS_URL`
46	   plus `Authorization: Bearer $ESHOBE_API_KEY`.
47	5. Call `GET /api/site` before first paint.
48	6. Render pages and blocks from `/api/pages`, `/api/posts`, `/api/products`, etc.
49	7. Resolve media from `site.media.origin + site.media.basePath`.
50	8. For stores, implement product, cart/checkout, and payment-method flows against the
51	   documented ecommerce endpoints.
52	9. Implement `GET /api/health` (or the manifest's `build.healthCheckPath`).
53	10. Implement `POST /api/revalidate` and verify the signed request.
54	11. If `proxiesApi: true`, proxy CMS-owned `/api/site`, `/api/pages`, `/api/posts`,
55	    `/api/products`, `/api/checkout`, `/api/payments/*`, `/api/media/file/*`, and
56	    other CMS endpoints back to `ESHOBE_CMS_URL` while keeping theme-owned routes
57	    such as your page renderer and `/api/revalidate` local.
58	12. Add a Dockerfile or build-pack-compatible package scripts.
59	13. Push the repository to GitHub.
60	14. Register the repository as a Theme in Eshobe CMS.
61	15. Sync the manifest.
62	16. Build an immutable GHCR artifact (recommended; CI setup and its three repository
63	    secrets are in [`theme-artifacts.md`](./theme-artifacts.md)) or let Coolify build from
64	    source.
65	17. Deploy preview.
66	18. Publish production only after health verification.
67	
68	Minimal repository layout:
69	
70	```text
71	my-eshobe-theme/
72	├── eshobe.theme.json
73	├── package.json
74	├── Dockerfile
75	├── src/
76	│   ├── cms/
77	│   │   ├── client.ts
78	│   │   ├── site.ts
79	│   │   └── types.ts
80	│   ├── app/
81	│   └── components/
82	└── README.md
83	```
84	
85	Minimal bootstrap client:
86	
87	```ts
88	import { formatPrice, themeCss } from '@eshobe/site-runtime'
89	
90	const cms = process.env.ESHOBE_CMS_URL ?? ''
91	const site = await fetch(`${cms || ''}/api/site`, {
92	  headers: process.env.ESHOBE_API_KEY
93	    ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ESHOBE_API_KEY}` }
94	    : {},
95	}).then((r) => r.json())
96	
97	const pages = await fetch(`${cms || ''}/api/pages?where[slug][equals]=home&locale=${site.defaultLocale}&depth=2`, {
98	  headers: process.env.ESHOBE_API_KEY
99	    ? { Authorization: `Bearer ${process.env.ESHOBE_API_KEY}` }
100	    : {},
101	}).then((r) => r.json())
102	
103	const css = themeCss(site.theme)
104	const price = formatPrice(180000, site.store.currency, site.defaultLocale)
105	```
106	
107	### Five calls to a working store
108	
109	```ts
110	// 1. Bootstrap — one call tells you tenant, locales, blocks, theme tokens and runtime settings.
111	const site = await fetch('https://CUSTOMER_DOMAIN/api/site').then(r => r.json())
112	
113	// 2. List products (public, Host-scoped, published only).
114	const products = await fetch(
115	  `https://CUSTOMER_DOMAIN/api/products?locale=${site.defaultLocale}&limit=12&sort=-createdAt&depth=1`,
116	).then(r => r.json())
117	
118	// 3. Render a price — NEVER interpolate product.price directly.
119	formatPrice(products.docs[0].price, site.store.currency, site.defaultLocale)
120	
121	// 4. Fetch and render a page's blocks.
122	const page = await fetch(`https://CUSTOMER_DOMAIN/api/pages?where[slug][equals]=home&locale=${site.defaultLocale}&depth=2`).then(r=>r.json())
123	
124	// 5. Checkout — collect name/phone and POST to the Host-scoped endpoint.
125	const checkout = await fetch('https://CUSTOMER_DOMAIN/api/checkout', {
126	  method:'POST',
127	  headers:{'content-type':'application/json'},
128	  body: JSON.stringify({ product: products.docs[0].id, quantity:1, name:'علی رضایی', phone:'09121234567' }),
129	}).then(r=>r.json())
130	```
131	
132	The rest of this document explains every field, edge case, and invariant behind those calls.

135	
136	## 2. Core Concepts
137	
138	### Multi-tenancy: one deployment, many sites
139	- One Postgres, one Next process. Every content row has a `site` FK to `sites`.
140	- Tenant is resolved from the **`Host` header** (`siteFromRequest` / `src/lib/site-query.ts`). No endpoint accepts `?site=` — that would be a leak.
141	- For headless clients **not on the customer's domain** (mobile app, POS, external renderer), tenant is resolved from **`Authorization: Bearer <site API key>`** (`role: "site"`). Host is tried first, key second.
142	- Anonymous REST reads are **scoped at the access layer** (`src/access/siteRead.ts`). A `where[site][equals]=OTHER_ID` is ANDed with the host's site and returns nothing. Verified by `tests/int/headless.int.spec.ts`.
143	
144	### Sites have a lifecycle, not a delete
145	`sites.status: "active" | "suspended" | "archived"`
146	- `active` → serves content.
147	- `suspended|archived` → every path returns a holding page (`SiteHolding`), 200 + `noindex`, no content. Do not delete a site (FK orphans, `cleanupAfterTenantDelete: false`).
148	
149	### Persian-first
150	- `defaultLocale = "fa"`, `rtl:true` on fa. `dir` comes from the locale per request, never hardcoded.
151	- Vazirmatn is the only font. Body `line-height` default 1.8.
152	- Every date → `formatDate()`, every number → `formatNumber()`, every price → `formatPrice()` — all in `@eshobe/site-runtime`. No raw `toLocaleDateString()`.
153	
154	### Money is integer minor units
155	- Stored price `120000` with `site.store.currency = "IRT"` means 120,000 Toman.
156	- Conversion `IRT ↔ IRR` lives exactly once in `src/lib/money.ts` (`1 تومان = 10 ریال`) — never in theme code.
157	- Product has **no** `currency` field; site does.
158	
159	### Pages vs Site Routes
160	- Pages collection holds CMS pages. Some URLs are **reserved site routes** that are not pages: `/posts`, `/posts/<slug>`, `/search`, `/checkout/<order>`, `/products/<slug>`. Saving a page with slug `posts` is rejected (`reservedPageSlug` hook). Resolve URLs through `resolveSiteRoute()` in `@eshobe/site-runtime/slug`.
161	
162	---
163	
164	## 3. Request Fundamentals
165	
166	### Base URL
167	```
168	https://<customer-domain>          # storefront (customer's own domain)
169	https://<control-plane-host>        # admin + Payload API (your deployment origin)
170	http://acme.localhost:3000          # local dev (Windows needs hosts entries via scripts/dev-hosts.ps1)
171	```
172	
173	### Host Header Is the Tenant
174	In dev/browser, `fetch('https://acme.localhost:3000/api/site')` automatically sends `Host: acme.localhost`. In server-to-server or AI agent code, explicitly set it:
175	
176	```ts
177	fetch('https://cms.example.com/api/site', {
178	  headers: { Host: 'acme.ir' } // tenant selection
179	})
180	// Or with API key (non-customer origin):
181	fetch('https://cms.example.com/api/site', {
182	  headers: { Authorization: 'Bearer eshobe_live_abc123...' }
183	})
184	```
185	
186	> **A deployed theme uses the key, not `Host`.** `ESHOBE_CMS_URL` is the CMS's public
187	> address, usually behind the same Coolify/Traefik proxy that serves the theme — and that
188	> proxy routes by `Host`. Rewriting `Host` to the customer domain sends the request back
189	> into the theme's own container (production) or to no router at all (preview): every
190	> lookup times out and the site renders empty. Send `Authorization: Bearer
191	> $ESHOBE_API_KEY` with the CMS's own `Host`. A site key scopes every public read —
192	> pages, posts, categories, header, footer, media — to its site, and also reads drafts,
193	> so filter `where[_status][equals]=published` yourself and never attach the key to
194	> visitor traffic other than draft-free reads (`/api/site`, `/api/media/file/*`).
195	
196	### CORS
197	`payload.config.ts` `cors: [ getServerSideURL(), ...API_CORS_ORIGINS ]`. Extra origins must be listed in `API_CORS_ORIGINS` env (comma-separated) to allow credentialed requests. No wildcard.
198	
199	### Common Query Params (Payload REST)
200	All collections share:
201	
202	
203	| Param | Example | Notes |
204	|-------|---------|-------|
205	| `locale` | `?locale=fa` | Active locale. Falls back to site's `defaultLocale` if omitted. Reads honor `fallback:true` |
206	| `fallbackLocale` | `&fallbackLocale=false` | Set `false` when enumerating hreflang/sitemap — otherwise untranslated slug returns Persian slug and advertises a 404 URL |
207	| `depth` | `&depth=1` | Populate relationships to this depth. `0` = ids only. Use `1` for media/images, `2` sparingly |
208	| `select` | `&select[title]=true&select[slug]=true` | Limit columns (also `defaultPopulate`) |
209	| `where` | `&where[slug][equals]=home` | See Payload where syntax below |
210	| `sort` | `&sort=-publishedAt` | `-` = desc |
211	| `limit` / `page` | `&limit=12&page=2` | `pagination:false` to disable |
212	| `draft` | `&draft=true` | Only with authenticated user/key (see auth). Anonymous drafts are always hidden |
213	| `overrideAccess` | — | **Never** on REST — Local API only, always `false` on frontend |
214	
215	### `where` Syntax (Payload)
216	```
217	where[field][operator]=value
218	operators: equals, not_equals, in, not_in, greater_than, less_than, like, exists
219	nest with and/or: where[and][0][slug][equals]=home
220	```
221	Example: pages by slug and published only is enforced server-side, but you write:
222	```
223	GET /api/pages?where[slug][equals]=درباره-ما&locale=fa
224	```
225	
226	### Auth Headers
227	
228	| Credential | Header | Access |
229	|------------|--------|--------|
230	| Anonymous visitor | _(none)_ | Published + tenant-scoped only |
231	| Logged-in Payload user | `Cookie: payload-token=...` or `Authorization: JWT ...` via `/api/users/login` | Drafts + own sites (multi-tenant plugin) |
232	| Site API key (`role:"site"`) | `Authorization: Bearer eshobe_live_...` | Its site's content incl. drafts, create/update on pages/posts/products, read/update status on orders |
233	| Platform API key (`role:"platform"`) | `Authorization: Bearer eshobe_live_...` | `GET /api/sites`, `POST /api/provision-site`, `POST /api/api-keys/*` — **no content** |
234	
235	Site key `id` is the `site` FK — the key **is** the tenant, not a filter.
236	
237	### Content-Type & Locale Digits
238	- POST bodies are JSON unless uploading media (`multipart/form-data`).
239	- Phone/price inputs accept Persian digits (`۰۹۱۲`) — `toAsciiDigits()` normalizes. Display with `toLocaleDigits()`.
240

244	
245	**The one call before first paint.** Returns per-tenant bootstrap so a headless renderer never hardcodes locales, blocks, currency or theme.
246	
247	### Request
248	```http
249	GET /api/site HTTP/1.1
250	Host: acme.ir

# Eshobe Theme Contract & Sibling-Theme Findings

## 1. `eshobe-cms/docs/THEME_API.md` — theme contract

**Version/stack:** `contractVersion = 1`; `GET /api/site` returns it; bump = breaking (L5-7). Payload 3.90 + Next 16 + Postgres + Tailwind v4, Persian-first, RTL default, multi-tenant via `Host` (L6).

**Required repo shape** (L68-83): `eshobe.theme.json`, `package.json`, `Dockerfile`, `src/cms/{client,site,types}.ts`, `src/app`, `src/components`, `README.md`. Build order + 17 steps L38-66.

**Tenancy (hard rules):** tenant from `Host` header (`siteFromRequest`) or `Authorization: Bearer <site key>`, never `?site=` / body field (L140-142, 1202-1213). Deployed themes must use the **key**, not `Host`, because `ESHOBE_CMS_URL` sits behind the same Host-routing proxy (L186-194). Anonymous reads ANDed with site constraint (L142).

**Endpoints / shapes**
- `GET /api/site` (L243-335). JSON fields: `availableLocales[]`, `blocks[]`, `contractVersion`, `defaultLocale`, `domain`, `branding{displayName,shortName,tagline,primaryLogo,compactLogo,homeLogo,lightLogo,darkLogo,favicon,socialImage,displayNameFa,logo,logoCompact,defaultOgImage}`, `media{basePath:"/api/media/file",origin}`, `name`, `slug`, `status`, `store{currency,paymentProvider}`, `theme{primary,accent,background,foreground,radius,lineHeight}`, `themeRuntime{theme.key,package.key,settings,bindings}`, `type` (L258-284). Key-resolved adds `id`, `domainVerified` (L287-290). `404 {"error":"unknown-host"}` (L297-300).
- Caching: `public, s-maxage=30, stale-while-revalidate=300`, `vary: Host`, `etag`, `last-modified`; key-resolved = `private, no-store` (L308-311).
- Payload REST envelope `{docs,totalDocs,limit,totalPages,page,pagingCounter,hasPrevPage,hasNextPage,prevPage,nextPage}` (L343-357). Query params `locale`, `fallbackLocale`, `depth`, `select`, `where`, `sort`, `limit/page`, `draft`; never `overrideAccess` (L199-213).
- Collections: `sites`,`pages`,`posts`,`products`,`orders`,`store`(global),`theme`(global),`media`,`categories`,`header`/`footer`(global),`forms`/`form-submissions`,`search`,`redirects` (L383-596). Product price = integer minor units of site currency; no `currency` on product (L154-157, 458-465).
- Checkout: `POST /api/checkout` body `{product(uuid),quantity,name,phone,email?,note?,company(honeypot)}`; 200 `{ok,redirectUrl,confirmationUrl}`, 503 `{ok,pending,confirmationUrl,message}`, 429 retry-after, 409 `{available}` or duplicate, 400 (L651-702). Callback `GET|POST /api/checkout/callback?order=`; receipt `/checkout/<id>?r=<HMAC sig>` (L710-740).
- Webhooks: `POST /api/revalidate`, `x-eshobe-signature: sha256=<HMAC-SHA256(secret, rawBody)>`, `x-eshobe-timestamp` **not signed**, body `{paths,resources,siteId,tags,timestamp}`; at-most-once, 3s (L1430-1440, 1847-1866). Health: `GET /api/health` cheap/local, IPv4, 200 (L1935-1945).
- Blocks: 14 slugs (`content,mediaBlock,cta,features,testimonials,faq,contact,formBlock,productGrid,gallery,team,pricing,logos,archive`), gated by site type (L760-777); per-block fields L783-903. Render `dir` from lexical `data.root.direction`; unknown blockType → warn+null (L905-908).
- Theming: `themeCss(theme)` emits body CSS vars; hex-validated, `readableOn` 0.179 luminance; logical utilities only (`ms/ps/text-start`) — `ml/pl/text-left` banned by eslint (L928-959).
- i18n: `locales` fa(rtl)/en, `defaultLocale='fa'`; `formatDate` (Jalali, Asia/Tehran), `formatNumber`, `formatPrice`, `toLocaleDigits`, `slugify`, `pagePath/postPath/productPath`, `resolveSiteRoute` (L989-1083); default locale unprefixed (L1067-1069).
- Media: `media.url` always relative; build `new URL(url, site.media.origin)`; sizes thumbnail 300w … og 1200×630 (L526-547, 1134-1145).
- Env vars platform-injected (L1489-1503): `ESHOBE_CMS_URL, ESHOBE_API_KEY, ESHOBE_SITE_ID, ESHOBE_SITE_DOMAIN, ESHOBE_DEFAULT_LOCALE, ESHOBE_LOCALES, ESHOBE_SITE_TYPE, ESHOBE_CURRENCY, ESHOBE_PUBLIC_ORIGIN, ESHOBE_REVALIDATE_SECRET, ESHOBE_CONTRACT_VERSION`; protected list L1700-1712.
- Manifest (§17b, L1540-1838): root `eshobe.theme.json`; fields `contractVersion,key,name,nameFa,siteTypes[],locales[],previewUrl,proxiesApi,capabilities,design{...},deployment{strategy,registryProvider,registryImageRepository,registryVisibility},build{buildPack,baseDirectory,dockerfileLocation,installCommand,buildCommand,startCommand,publishDirectory,port,healthCheckPath,isStatic},env[{key,source,required,secret,labelFa,help}],settings{...},contentSlots[{key,type,required,labelFa,labelEn,help}]`. Unknown `build`/`design`/`deployment` keys **reject** the manifest (`key` regex `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/`, env ≤50, slots ≤50). Bindings: look up by `id`, routes are the theme's, slug only a first-run hint, one canonical URL (L1817-1841).

## 2. `theme-deployments.md`
Coolify-first production; legacy `edge` behind `ESHOBE_LEGACY_CADDY_EDGE=1` (L12-14). Lanes `preview|production` (L111-120); 6-step readiness flow (L24-31). Lifecycle `queued→creating→building→verifying→live|failed` (L188-258). Promotion probe hits the app's own hostname at `healthCheckPath` (else `/`), IPv4 loopback, 2xx only, 3xx only on `/` fallback, retries `DEPLOY_HEALTH_*`, 10-min deadline (L221-231). Failed deploy changes nothing but its row (L252-258). Env/tenant settings via `GET|POST /api/site-theme-settings/current?site=<id>` (L325). Secrets AES-256-GCM; key rotates invalidate (L417-429). Port 3000 default, `health_check_host: 127.0.0.1` pin.

## 3. `theme-artifacts.md`
Two strategies `coolify_build` / `registry_image`; prefer registry (L11-20). Workflow checkout→validate manifest→install→lint→typecheck→tests→build→smoke→Buildx→GHCR→inspect digest→register (L28-30). CI secrets: `ESHOBE_CMS_URL`, `ESHOBE_THEME_ARTIFACT_SECRET`, `ESHOBE_THEME_PACKAGE_ID` (L47-56). `POST /api/platform/theme-packages/<uuid>/artifacts`, header `X-Eshobe-Signature-256`, body `{repository,ref,commit,registry:"ghcr",image,tag,digest,workflowRunId,workflowRunUrl,platform}`; 201/200/400/401/404/422/503 (L89-122). Deploy always `ghcr.io/owner/image@sha256:<digest>` (L30, 163-184).

No Radix-Select etc. needed for corporate; it uses radix accordion/dialog/slot, cva, clsx, lucide, motion, tailwind-merge.

## 6. Sibling comparison
**`cms-resturant-theme`** (key `immersive-restaurant`): `siteTypes:["store"]`, `capabilities.commerce:true`, `env:[]`, same `Dockerfile`/`/api/health`, settings mostly boolean/select (animation/scene). It vendors `@eshobe/site-runtime` as a real workspace package (`packages/site-runtime`, `workspace:*`, exports pointing at `src/*.ts`). Conventions: `src/lib/site.ts` for origin/canonical/nav, `src/lib/theme/settings.ts` + `palette.ts`, `src/lib/routes.ts` + `i18n.ts`, `src/lib/media.ts`, `x-theme-locale` header (not `x-lw-locale`), `export const dynamic='force-dynamic'` + `getSite()` at request time, `@fontsource-variable/vazirmatn` instead of a font generator, purchase form under `components/commerce/PurchaseForm.tsx`, plus `fixtures/cms/server.ts` and `validate:manifest` script.

**`cms-portfolio2-theme`** (key `meridian`): `siteTypes:["portfolio"]`, `locales:["en"]`, single-locale, fixed Next routes (`app/about`, `app/projects/[slug]`, `app/objects`, `app/careers`) plus its own `api/site` and `api/content` endpoints, a `loadSnapshot()` that fetches `/api/site` then resolves `themeRuntime.bindings` by id with `/api/pages/<id>?depth=2` (`src/lib/cms/source.ts:18-52`). No `@eshobe/site-runtime`; uses `next/font/google` Geist, drizzle/pg template leftovers, `tsx --test` instead of vitest, and a large settings surface (labels, clocks, timezones, socials) rather than page-slug settings. It is the least contract-aligned of the three; treat arch2 as the reference.
